newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: EU to press WTO case against US on Cuba-Brittan.
newsitem.headline: EU to press WTO case against US on Cuba-Brittan.

text.p: European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said on Saturday Brussels would push ahead with a World Trade Organisation case against the United States over its Helms-Burton law on Cuba if there was no U.S. row-back.

Brittan told a news conference the EU still had full support from nearly all other members of the WTO for its action over the law, which aims to restrict foreign investment in the communist island's economy.
Members of a WTO dispute panel, he said, would be named on February 20 "in the absence of offers (from the United States) that are better than we have had so far."

Brussels had earlier asked WTO Director-General Renato Ruggiero to nominate the panel -- which will have six months to return its findings -- after the United States declined to approve names proposed by the trade body Secretariat.
But last week the EU requested Ruggiero to hold back until February 20, saying it was making a further effort in direct talks to get an agreement with Washington.

But Brittan said on Saturday those talks so far had not produced anything that was "satisfactory to meet our concerns." He said Brussels rejected U.S. assertions that it was acting over Helms-Burton in defence of national sovereignty.
